title: The Illicit World of Sea Cucumbers
gist: Sea cucumbers, retailing for up to $3,000 per kilogram in Asia, have become a cash substitute for criminal groups — including payment between Chinese fentanyl-precursor makers and Mexican cartels — driving illegal harvesting from Mexico to India and Sri Lanka. China's massive aquaculture build-out and FAO influence shape the legal trade, while Beijing's renewed ban on Japanese seafood has cut off Japan's fisheries and may push trade toward the yakuza.

insights.claim: Former U.S. Border Patrol agent Cesar Daleo acted as middleman between Chinese chemical manufacturers and Mexican cartels, moving fentanyl precursors one way and being paid in sea cucumbers — smuggling protected Isostichopus fuscus worth over $250,000 on at least 80 occasions between 2014 and 2016.

insights.claim: Over the past two decades the Sinaloa Cartel and, to a lesser extent, the Jalisco New Generation Cartel have encroached on Mexican fisheries, inserting themselves between Chinese buyers and fishermen through kidnappings, threats and buyouts; sea cucumber seizures at the southern U.S. border have more than doubled since 2018.
